spi_protocol.mode: SPI mode 0 (CPOL 0, CPHA 0): COPI sampled on rising SCK, CIPO changes after falling SCK; SCK idles low
spi_protocol.bit_order: MSB first in both directions (mom/rtl/hydra_tt_spi.sv:22,119,133; cipo = tx_sr[7] line 91)
spi_protocol.speed: SCK below clk/8 (hydra_tt_spi.sv:14-15); the cocotb host uses clk/10 (tt/tile/test/test.py:71)
spi_protocol.oversampling: SCK, COPI and CSn are synchronised into clk (same depth, hydra_tt_spi.sv:62-80); edges are detected in clk, so COPI must be stable around the SCK rise and the host should sample CIPO at its rising edge, at least ~4 clk after the falling edge (DERIVED from 128-139)
spi_protocol.command_byte: byte 0 = {rw, addr[6:0]}; rw = 1 read, 0 write (tt/tile/src/rtl/hydra_tt_regs.sv:239-242). While it shifts in, CIPO returns STATUS[15:8] (386).
spi_protocol.write_frame: CSn low, command byte (rw=0), exactly LEN data bytes MSB first, CSn high. Length in bits = 8 + 8*LEN: ID n/a (RO), WD 136, CTRL 16, ACTION 16, COMP 16, FENCE 16, PARAM 56, GLOBAL 24. Commits at the cs_end pulse after CSn rises (205-208, 259-286).
spi_protocol.read_frame: CSn low, command byte (rw=1), then N dummy bytes; data byte k (k = 0 first) = value[(LEN-1-k)*8 +: 8] (369-376, 386-387). Length in bits = 8 + 8*LEN for a full read: ID 40, WD 136, CTRL 16, STATUS 24, RESULT 56, CALUPD 24, BUSY 24, FENCE 16, GLOBAL 24, INFO 16. Any length is legal; bytes past LEN read 0x00; COPI content after the command byte is ignored. Registers of <= 6 bytes are one snapshot taken when data byte 0 is loaded (380-387); WD (and chip LASTWD) are live.
spi_protocol.csn_deassert_mid_frame: Partial bits of the last byte are discarded (rx_valid only on the 8th bit, hydra_tt_spi.sv:121-127). For a write, the number of whole data bytes != LEN -> nothing committed, FRAME_ERR set (205-207, 262); for WD the bytes already shifted stay in wd_q but WD_OK was cleared at the command byte, so GO is refused with GO_ERR. A frame with no complete byte is ignored with no error. A read cut short has no side effect.
spi_protocol.wrong_length: Too short or too long write -> FRAME_ERR, no change (n_data must equal reg_len, 205-206; n_data saturates at 31, 248). Write to RO or unmapped address -> FRAME_ERR (161-163). Reads never error.
spi_protocol.frame_errors_are_sticky: FRAME_ERR (STATUS[8]) stays set until ACTION.CLEAR_STICKY (312-315) and drives IRQ (394).
spi_protocol.cipo_change_edge: synchronised falling SCK; first bit of each byte is loaded on CSn fall or on the falling edge after a byte boundary (hydra_tt_spi.sv:112-116, 128-135, 139)

worked_example.scope: Tile (tt_um_hydra_mom, NENG 5, NTAG 4). Every byte below is VERIFIED-SIM on tt/tile/src/project.v with SCK = clk/10; the cycle counts are from that run.

steps.bytes: Hold rst_n low >= 1 clk with CSn (ui[2]) high, release, wait >= 3 clk.

steps.action: Stage the descriptor: GEMM, INT8, LAT_BALANCED, PWR_BALANCED, M=N=K=4, bytes=48, src_loc 0, tag 0
steps.meaning: one 17-byte frame to WD (0x01): 16 data bytes MSB first = 0x30A00080008000800006000000000000. Field positions from mom_pkg.sv:143-155: op_class[127:124]=3, dtype[123:121]=0, lat[120:119]=1, pwr[118:117]=1, dim_m[116:101]=4, dim_n[100:85]=4, dim_k[84:69]=4, bytes[68:45]=48, tag[42:35]=0. WD is one 128-bit register; there is no per-word staging.
ACTION bit 0. Commit at cs_end (cycle 2528); mom_features takes the descriptor at 2529; the shared cost engine sweeps 5 engines x 2 cycles; dispatch at 2541 (13 cycles after cs_end).
STATUS = 0xD840 = READY | ANY_BUSY | WD_OK | DISPATCHED | FENCE_BUSY (FENCE=0 = tag 0, busy). The leading 0x10 is the live STATUS[15:8] at frame start, taken mid-decision.

RESULT = 0x200000002000: engine = 0x20>>5 = 1 (SIMD), tag = (0x20>>1)&0xF = 0, margin = 0x00000020 = 32 (TPU 71 - SIMD 39), err_tag 0. Pins: uo_out 0xE6, uio_out 0x60 (margin nibble 6 = 1+floor(log2 32)).
comp_valid at cs_end+1 (3829); scoreboard measured 3829 - 2541 = 1288 cycles vs t_pred 27; calibration raises k[SIMD][GEMM] 64 -> 68 at 3830.
one update; STATUS[15:8] 0x98 = READY | WD_OK | DISPATCHED (no tag busy)

steps.action: Rejected malformed frame: two data bytes to the one-byte CTRL register
steps.meaning: n_data = 2 != reg_len 1 -> nothing committed (HOLD would have stayed 0 anyway, the 0x01 byte is NOT applied), FRAME_ERR set.
STATUS = 0x9900: FRAME_ERR (bit 8) set; CTRL reads 0 (TX 82 00 -> RX 99 00)

worked_example.follow_on: Same session, GEMM INT8 8x8x8 bytes 192 (TX 01 30 A0 01 00 01 00 01 00 00 18 00 00 00 00 00 00, then 03 01, then 86 x6): RX ... 40 00 00 00 91 00 -> engine 2 (TPU), tag 0, margin 145 (SIMD now 246 because k = 68; from a fresh reset the margin is 136). VERIFIED-SIM.

calibration_rule.format: 8-bit unsigned Q2.6 per (engine, op class); 64 = 1.0 (mom_pkg.sv:275-276; mom_calibrate.sv:146-148)
calibration_rule.table_size: NENG x 9 entries (5 x 9 = 45 bytes on the tile)
calibration_rule.applied_in_cost: t_cal = floor(m*k/64) << e, with t_pred normalised to a 16-bit mantissa m by e in {0, 8, 16}; exact below 2^16, at most 1/256 low above (mom_cost_engine.sv:278-303)
calibration_rule.update_compare: t_cal_ref = floor(t_predicted * k / 64) computed at 34 bits (40-bit product >> 6) (mom_calibrate.sv:179-180); too_slow = t_measured > t_cal_ref; too_fast = t_measured < t_cal_ref; equal -> no move (184-185, 220)
calibration_rule.bounds: up: min(k + step, 255); down: max(k - step, 4) (202-216)
calibration_rule.when_applied: on scoreboard cal_valid (one cycle after an accepted completion), unless CAL_FREEZE, t_predicted == 0, or engine/op class out of range (224); CAL_RESET (level) has priority and forces all k = 64 and the count to 0 (233-237)
calibration_rule.counter: upd_count +1 per applied update (240), readable as CALUPD
calibration_rule.numeric_example: VERIFIED-SIM: k = 64, t_predicted = 27, t_measured = 1288: t_cal_ref = 27*64>>6 = 27 < 1288 -> k = 64 + (64>>4) = 68. DERIVED: k = 250 too slow -> 250 + 15 = 265 -> clamped 255; k = 4 too fast -> step max(0,1) = 1 -> 3 -> clamped 4; from 64, repeated too-slow updates give 68, 72, 76, 80, 85, 90, 95, 100, 106, 112, 119, 126, 133 (k reaches 2x = 128+ after 13 updates).

scoreboard_rules.allocation_order: lowest-numbered free tag (priority loop from NTAG-1 down to 0, last match wins; mom_scoreboard.sv:140-150); tile tags 0..3
scoreboard_rules.exhaustion: no free tag -> disp_ready 0 (177); the descriptor waits in mom_top's cost register; further GOs fill the features register and the pending request; READY drops; nothing is dropped and dispatch resumes by itself when a tag is freed (VERIFIED by test_tag_exhaustion_and_recovery and my sim)
scoreboard_rules.engine_full: queue_depth >= QMAX (214) blocks dispatch to that engine and marks it !valid at costing; on the tile QMAX = NTAG = 4. Because the mask is computed once per sweep, a descriptor whose only capable engines were full when costed is never dispatched (deadlock, see mom_top failure)
scoreboard_rules.out_of_order_completion: any busy tag may complete at any time, in any order (do_comp depends only on busy[comp_tag], 181); dispatch and completion on the same engine in the same cycle net to zero (208-211)
scoreboard_rules.stale_or_invalid_completion: tag >= NTAG or not busy: ignored (no tag freed, no counter change, no calibration sample) and err_stale_comp pulses next cycle -> STATUS.STALE sticky + IRQ (172, 181, 187-191; regs 310). VERIFIED-SIM: COMP tag 3 while free -> STATUS 0xC240
scoreboard_rules.fence: fence_busy = busy[FENCE] if FENCE < NTAG, else 0 (260)
scoreboard_rules.measured_time: now - t_start, 32-bit modulo (252); t_pred stored is the uncalibrated prediction of the chosen engine (mom_top.sv:411)

systolic_dataflow.summary:
Output-stationary 4 x 4 (N_PE = 4) INT8 array. Each processing element PE(r,c) owns one 32-bit accumulator
(tpu_pe.sv:29) and computes one result element; A operands enter on the WEST edge (one per physical row) and
move east one PE per array step; B operands enter on the NORTH edge (one per column) and move south one PE per
step (tpu_array.sv:31-35,41-44). Nothing enters from the south or east.
systolic_dataflow.operand_order:
Slice k (one per handshake) = column k of A (op_a[i] = a[i][k]) and row k of B (op_b[j] = b[k][j]) (tpu_top.sv:30, 57-58).
tpu_top reverses the A lanes: logical row i drives physical row N-1-i (tpu_top.sv:121-124), because the drain
empties the bottom physical row first and that must be logical row 0.
systolic_dataflow.skew:
tpu_feeder delays west lane r by r steps and north lane c by c steps; lane 0 is combinational (tpu_feeder.sv:30-62).
Each PE hop adds one more registered step (tpu_pe.sv:40-41). Slice k therefore reaches PE(r,c) r + c steps after it
is consumed, from both directions at once: a[N-1-r][k] meets b[k][c] there and PE(r,c) accumulates
C[N-1-r][c]. Steps happen only when arr_en = 1 (op_valid in STREAM, always in FLUSH) (tpu_ctrl.sv:153), so a stall
freezes feeder, operand registers and accumulators together.
systolic_dataflow.cycle_timeline_4x4_K4:
Simulated (tb_c_tpu), +n = edges after the accept cycle, operand every cycle:
  +0 accept (IDLE); +1 CLEAR (all accumulators 0, feeder flushed) (tpu_ctrl.sv:148,156; tpu_pe.sv:46)
  +2..+5 STREAM: slice k=0..3 consumed at +2+k
  PE(r,c) performs its MAC for slice k at +2+k+r+c. PE(0,0): +2..+5; far corner PE(3,3): +8..+11.
  Observed west edge (lanes 0..3) at +2: 10,0,0,0; +3: -10,-1,0,0; +4: 20,-2,5,0; +5: -20,-3,6,1;
  +6: 0,-4,7,2; +7: 0,0,8,3; +8: 0,0,0,4 (logical row 3 = [10,-10,20,-20] on physical row 0, logical row 0 = [1,2,3,4] on row 3).
  Observed north edge at +2: 1,0,0,0; +3: 0,0,0,0; +4: 4,1,2,0; +5: -5,-2,-3,-1; +6: 0,3,1,2; +7: 0,0,0,0; +8: 0,0,0,1.
  +6..+11 FLUSH: 2N-2 = 6 more steps, zeros injected (feed_valid = 0), so the last operands reach PE(3,3) (tpu_ctrl.sv:113-126).
  +12 first DRAIN shift: every accumulator copies the one above, top row gets 0 (tpu_pe.sv:47, tpu_array.sv:37); the
  bottom row's old values (logical row 0) are captured by tpu_drain the same edge.
  +13..+16 results C[0][0..3]; shifts at +17, +22, +27 (N+1 = 5 cycles per row); results +18..+21, +23..+26, +28..+31.
  +28..+32 TAIL until the serialiser is empty; +33 DONE pulse; +34 ready.
systolic_dataflow.cycles_for_N_by_N_tile:
No stalls: K + N^2 + 3N + 1 cycles from acceptance to the done pulse (CLEAR 1, STREAM K, FLUSH 2N-2, DRAIN
(N-1)(N+1)+1, TAIL N+1, DONE). N=4, K=4 -> 33 (simulated). Last MAC at +(K + 2N - 1); first result at +(K + 2N + 1).
Each cycle op_valid is low during STREAM adds one cycle.
systolic_dataflow.accumulators: In each PE (acc_q, tpu_pe.sv:29), 32-bit, cleared by CLEAR; never move during compute.
systolic_dataflow.drain:
Column shift south, bottom row out (tpu_array.sv:47-49) -> tpu_drain serialises lane 0..3, so the stream is row-major
C[0][0], C[0][1], ... C[3][3] with res_last on the 16th (tpu_drain.sv:45-47). All N*N results are always drained,
even for M or N < 4 (lanes outside must be zero-fed).

ntt_butterfly.form: Cooley-Tukey (decimation-in-time style) butterfly: twiddle multiplies b BEFORE the add/subtract.
ntt_butterfly.equations:
v  = b * w mod q            (ntt_modmul, Barrett)
y0 = (a + v) mod q          sum = a + v; y0 = sum >= q ? sum - q : sum
y1 = (a - v) mod q          diff = a + q - v; y1 = diff >= q ? diff - q : diff
Barrett: t = b*w; u = (t * BM) >> BSH; r = t - u*q; v = r >= q ? r - q : r, with BSH = 2*QW, BM = floor(2^BSH / q).

ntt_butterfly.barrett_margin:
Exhaustive C sweep over all residue pairs: max r = 4865 (q=3329, limit 2q=6658) and 16089 (q=12289, limit 24578).
With BM-1 (the 'equivalent' mutation): q=12289 max r = 22862 < 24578 (still equivalent), but q=3329 max r = 7058 > 6658
on 4541 pairs - the mutation is a real fault at 3329. The suite only runs it at the default modulus (mutate_ntt.py:12-19).

rst_sync.design: STAGES=2 flops, both cleared asynchronously by arst_n; on each clk edge sync_q shifts in a constant 1; rst_n = sync_q[1] (lines 27-32). Assertion is immediate (combinational path from arst_n through the async clear); release happens on the 2nd rising clk edge after arst_n rises.
rst_sync.where_used: Every generated FPGA top (e.g. fpga/build/basys3/hydra_basys3_tt.sv:49-50), the OpenFrame top (hydra_openframe_top.sv:125-126), inside hydra_mom_pins (mom/hydra_mom_pins.sv:132-134) and the TT tile (tt_um_hydra_mom.sv:141-143). Not used by hydra_basys3_selftest (own POR counter, lines 60-67) or inside hydra_sys_tile (reset comes from the bridge's registered tile_rst_n, hydra_fpga_bridge.sv:172).
animation_sequence: t1: arst_n rises between clock edges; sync_q still 00
edge 1: sync_q=01 (flop 0 sampled the constant 1; this is the flop that may go metastable if arst_n release is near the edge)
edge 2: sync_q=11 -> rst_n=1, released synchronously to clk
rst_sync.proof: hydra_rst_sync.sby prove depth 8: immediate assert and release only after STAGES clean edges, scan_mode assumed 0 (hydra_rst_sync.sv:34-47)

jtag_handshake.modules: hydra_jtag_tap -> hydra_jtag_bridge (dbg/rtl/hydra_jtag_bridge.sv:52-171), as wired in fpga/rtl/hydra_fpga_jtag_host.sv:71-86
jtag_handshake.protocol: toggle request / toggle acknowledge (not 4-phase req-ack); one transfer in flight; payload not synchronised
jtag_handshake.synchroniser_flops: 4 in total: req_sync[1:0] in the clk domain (line 125) and ack_sync[1:0] in the TCK domain (line 90). Payload (rw_q, addr_q, wdata_q TCK->clk; rdata_sys clk->TCK) crosses with no synchroniser, held stable by the handshake.

signals.tck_domain: user_update (from TAP), req_tog, busy, rw_q, addr_q, wdata_q, ack_sync[1:0], ack_tog, rdata_q, user_capture={busy,addr_q,rdata_q}
signals.clk_domain: req_sync[1:0], req_seen, req_edge=req_sync[1]^req_seen, reg_we/reg_re/reg_addr/reg_wdata, reg_we_q/reg_re_q, rdata_sys, ack_tog_sys

sequence: TCK edge T0: TAP in UPDATE_DR with IR=USER -> user_dr <= shifted value, user_update <= 1 (hydra_jtag_tap.sv:155-159)
TCK edge T1: bridge sees user_update && !busy -> rw_q/addr_q/wdata_q captured, req_tog flips, busy=1 (bridge 97-105)
clk edge C1: req_sync[0] <= req_tog (first synchroniser flop) (line 125)
clk edge C2: req_sync[1] <= req_sync[0]; now req_edge = req_sync[1] ^ req_seen = 1 (line 117)
clk edge C3: req_seen <= req_sync[1]; reg_addr/reg_wdata <= payload; reg_we <= rw_q or reg_re <= !rw_q, for one clk (lines 129-134)
clk edge C4: reg_we_q/reg_re_q <= 1 (lines 145-149); the register file has answered reg_rdata
clk edge C5: read: rdata_sys <= reg_rdata and ack_tog_sys flips; write: ack_tog_sys flips (lines 135-141)
TCK edge T3: ack_sync[1] <= ack_sync[0]; ack_edge = ack_sync[1] ^ ack_tog = 1 (line 83)
TCK edge T4: ack_tog <= ack_sync[1], rdata_q <= rdata_sys, busy <= 0 (lines 92-96)
Next DR scan: CAPTURE_DR loads user_capture = {busy=0, addr_q, rdata_q} for the probe (hydra_jtag_tap.sv:147-149; bridge 109)
jtag_handshake.not_handled: Stopped system clock -> busy stays 1 forever; TCK stopped -> result parks until TCK resumes (bridge 42-48). TAP reset can produce one phantom read of addr 0 (see jtag_bridge.failure).
jtag_handshake.verification: Simulation with tck 35 ns and clk 10 ns (fixed 7:2 ratio) (dbg/tb/tb_jtag_bridge.sv:21-22); structural text check dbg/formal/cdc_check.py; the bridge's in-RTL FORMAL asserts are not run by any .sby

reset_and_cdc.animation_caveat: An animation of these sequences shows the intended logical order of events only. It is not evidence about metastability: event simulation (and these formal models) treat flops as resolving instantly, which is exactly why removing a synchroniser stage is invisible to simulation (dbg/formal/cdc_check.py:7-18). Real resolution time, MTBF and the safety of the unsynchronised payload depend on silicon/FPGA timing and constraints, which nothing here proves.
